name: Perseverance
tagline: I search for signs of ancient life and keep samples so they can one day be brought back to Earth.
discovery: I explored the delta of an ancient lake in Jezero crater and filled tubes with rock samples, some of them left on the ground awaiting a future return to Earth. My MOXIE instrument even made oxygen from the Martian air, a first.
status_note: Still active: I am exploring the rim of Jezero crater, looking for the oldest rocks.

presentation.title: My name already says it all: I'm Perseverance.
presentation.body: I'm a rover from the Mars 2020 mission. I search for signs of ancient life and keep samples so they can one day be brought back to Earth.

chapters.title: A sign seeker
chapters.body: I look like my big brother Curiosity, but my mission is different: to search for signs of ancient microbial life, and set aside the best rocks in sealed tubes.

chapters.title: A passenger under my belly
chapters.body: On 30 July 2020, I lift off from Florida. Under my belly, I carry a passenger: the little Ingenuity helicopter.

chapters.title: Landing in an ancient lake
chapters.body: On 18 February 2021, I land in Jezero crater. Billions of years ago, a river poured into it and built a delta: the perfect place to look for signs of life.

chapters.title: Oxygen on Mars
chapters.body: On 20 April 2021, my MOXIE instrument turns some of the carbon dioxide in the Martian air into oxygen. A first! One day, this technology could help astronauts breathe or make fuel.

chapters.title: A sample depot
chapters.body: In late 2022, I leave ten sample tubes on the ground at a place called Three Forks. It is a backup stash, waiting for a future mission to come and collect it.

chapters.title: Still on the road
chapters.body: Today, I am exploring the crater rim. Every rock I study helps answer a huge question: has life ever existed beyond Earth?

quiz.question: Which passenger did Perseverance take to Mars?
quiz.explanation: Ingenuity travelled under its belly. It became the first aircraft to fly on another planet.

quiz.question: What did the MOXIE instrument make on Mars?
quiz.explanation: MOXIE turned carbon dioxide from the Martian air into oxygen: a first on another planet.
